CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS downloaded_ambient_sounds (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        sound_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
        remote_key TEXT NOT NULL,
        relative_path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
        category_key TEXT NOT NULL,
        name TEXT NOT NULL,
        file_path TEXT NOT NULL,
        downloaded_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        last_accessed_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        title TEXT NOT NULL,
        content TEXT,
        color TEXT,
        sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        created_at DATETIME,
        updated_at DATETIME
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS progress (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        word_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
        times_played INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        times_correct INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        last_played DATETIME,
        familiarity REAL DEFAULT 0,
        ease_factor REAL DEFAULT 2.5,
        interval_days INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        next_review DATETIME,
        consecutive_correct INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        memory_state TEXT DEFAULT 'new',
        FOREIGN KEY (word_id) REFERENCES words(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        UNIQUE(word_id)
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS timer_records (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        start_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
        duration_minutes INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        focus_duration_minutes INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        break_duration_minutes INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        rounds_completed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        focus_minutes INTEGER DEFAULT 25,
        break_minutes INTEGER DEFAULT 5,
        is_partial INTEGER DEFAULT 0
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        content TEXT NOT NULL,
        completed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        deferred INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        priority INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        category TEXT,
        note TEXT,
        color TEXT,
        sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        due_at DATETIME,
        alarm_enabled INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        sync_to_system_calendar INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
        system_calendar_notification_enabled INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
        system_calendar_notification_minutes_before INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        system_calendar_alarm_enabled INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        system_calendar_alarm_minutes_before INTEGER DEFAULT 10,
        created_at DATETIME,
        completed_at DATETIME
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_marks (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        word_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
        type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(type IN ('new', 'important', 'mastered')),
        note TEXT,
        created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        FOREIGN KEY (word_id) REFERENCES words(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        UNIQUE(word_id, type)
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS word_field_media (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        word_field_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
        media_type TEXT NOT NULL,
        media_source TEXT NOT NULL,
        media_label TEXT,
        mime_type TEXT,
        sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        FOREIGN KEY (word_field_id) REFERENCES word_fields(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS word_field_styles (
        word_field_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
        background_hex TEXT,
        border_hex TEXT,
        text_hex TEXT,
        accent_hex TEXT,
        FOREIGN KEY (word_field_id) REFERENCES word_fields(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS word_field_tags (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        word_field_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
        tag TEXT NOT NULL,
        sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        FOREIGN KEY (word_field_id) REFERENCES word_fields(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS word_fields (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        word_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
        field_key TEXT NOT NULL,
        field_label TEXT NOT NULL,
        field_value_json TEXT NOT NULL,
        style_json TEXT,
        sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        FOREIGN KEY (word_id) REFERENCES words(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS word_memory_events (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        word_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
        event_kind TEXT NOT NULL,
        quality INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        weak_reasons_json TEXT,
        session_title TEXT,
        created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        FOREIGN KEY (word_id) REFERENCES words(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wordbooks (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        name TEXT NOT NULL,
        path TEXT UNIQUE,
        word_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        schema_version TEXT,
        metadata_json TEXT,
        created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
      );

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS words (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        wordbook_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
        entry_uid TEXT,
        word TEXT NOT NULL,
        meaning TEXT,
        primary_gloss TEXT,
        search_word TEXT NOT NULL,
        search_meaning TEXT,
        search_details TEXT,
        search_word_compact TEXT NOT NULL,
        search_details_compact TEXT,
        schema_version TEXT,
        source_payload_json TEXT,
        sort_index INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        extension_json TEXT,
        entry_json TEXT,
        FOREIGN KEY (wordbook_id) REFERENCES wordbooks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
      );

排队、满场、闭馆、下雨和临时取消都很常见。真正降低决策压力的方法，是在同一片区域预留一个替代点，而不是让整次外出因为一个点失败而中断。

如果某件事听起来太大，就把它改成 5 分钟版本。每日抉择的价值是破冰，不是替你安排完整人生。

s copy of the executable will launch
# correctly, since the resources must in the right relative locations. To avoid
# people trying to run the unbundled copy, put it in a subdirectory instead of
# the default top-level location.
set_target_properties(${BINARY_NAME}
  PROPERTIES
  RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/intermediates_do_not_run"
)


# Generated plugin build rules, which manage building the plugins and adding
# them to the application.
include(flutter/generated_plugins.cmake)


# === Installation ===
# By default, "installing" just makes a relocatable bundle in the build
# directory.
set(BUILD_BUNDLE_DIR "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/bundle")
if(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX_INITIALIZED_TO_DEFAULT)
  set(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX "${BUILD_BUNDLE_DIR}" CACHE PATH "..." FORCE)
endif()

# Start with a clean build bundle directory every time.
install(CODE "
  file(REMOVE_RECURSE "${BUILD_BUNDLE_DIR}/")
  " COMPONENT Runtime)

set(INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/data")
set(INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/lib")

install(TARGETS ${BINARY_NAME} RUNTIME DESTINATION "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}"
  COMPONENT Runtime)

install(FILES "${FLUTTER_ICU_DATA_FILE}" DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR}"
  COMPONENT Runtime)

install(FILES "${FLUTTER_LIBRARY}" DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR}"
  COMPONENT Runtime)

foreach(bundled_library ${PLUGIN_BUNDLED_LIBRARIES})
  install(FILES "${bundled_library}"
    DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR}"
    COMPONENT Runtime)
endforeach(bundled_library)

# Copy the native assets provided by the build.dart from all packages.
set(NATIVE_ASSETS_DIR "${PROJECT_BUILD_DIR}native_assets/linux/")
install(DIRECTORY "${NATIVE_ASSETS_DIR}"
   DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR}"
   COMPONENT Runtime)

# Fully re-copy the assets directory on each build to avoid having stale files
# from a previous install.
set(FLUTTER_ASSET_DIR_NAME "flutter_assets")
install(CODE "
  file(REMOVE_RECURSE "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR}/${FLUTTER_ASSET_DIR_NAME}")
  " COMPONENT Runtime)
install(DIRECTORY "${PROJECT_BUILD_DIR}/${FLUTTER_ASSET_DIR_NAME}"
  DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_DATA_DIR}" COMPONENT Runtime)

# Install the AOT library on non-Debug builds only.
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE MATCHES "Debug")
  install(FILES "${AOT_LIBRARY}" DESTINATION "${INSTALL_BUNDLE_LIB_DIR}"
    COMPONENT Runtime)
endif()

Keep the bedroom cool, dark, and quiet. Try a temperature of 18-20°C.

The ideal bedroom temperature for sleep is 18-20°C (65-68°F). Core body temperature must drop by about 1°C to initiate and maintain sleep. A room that is too warm prevents this drop. Noise above 40dB can cause arousals even without full awakening.
Temperature, noise, and light are the three main environmental factors affecting sleep quality.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.caffeine: Set a personal caffeine cutoff 8-10 hours before your typical bedtime.

Adenosine builds up during the day, creating "sleep pressure." Caffeine temporarily blocks adenosine receptors, masking sleepiness without reducing the underlying pressure. Genetic differences in CYP1A2 mean some people metabolize caffeine much slower than others.
Caffeine works by blocking adenosine receptors. Its half-life is 3-7 hours, meaning a 2pm coffee can still affect sleep at midnight.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.diary_tr: Log just 3 data points per night: bedtime, wake time, and how rested you feel.

Consumer sleep trackers estimate sleep stages from movement and heart rate, but their accuracy varies widely and they often overestimate sleep. A simple diary capturing bedtime, wake time, and subjective restfulness provides complementary data that highlights behavioral patterns trackers cannot see.
A 30-second sleep log reveals patterns that even detailed sleep trackers miss.
The power of a simple sleep diary
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.digital_: Switch devices to night mode after sunset. Stop active screen use 30-60 minutes before bed.

The melanopsin photopigment in ipRGC cells is most sensitive to ~480nm (blue) light. Evening exposure shifts the circadian clock later, making it harder to fall asleep. However, the effect size varies widely between individuals, and content arousal may matter as much as the light itself.
Evening screen light, especially blue wavelengths, can suppress melatonin by activating the same ipRGC cells that respond to morning light.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.light.ac: Get outside within 30 minutes of waking. No sunglasses for the first 10 minutes.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.light.de: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) uses light detected by ipRGC cells in the retina to synchronize your circadian rhythm. Morning light advances your clock, making it easier to fall asleep at night. Even 10-15 minutes outdoors on a cloudy day provides enough lux to make a measurable difference.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.light.su: Bright light within 30 minutes of waking is the single strongest signal for your internal clock.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.nap.acti: Naps under 20 minutes, before 3pm. If you have insomnia, skip naps entirely.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.nap.deta: The ideal nap window is 10-20 minutes (the "power nap") which stays in lighter NREM sleep stages before entering deep slow-wave sleep. Longer naps (30+ min) risk sleep inertia—grogginess on waking—and can reduce homeostatic sleep pressure, making it harder to fall asleep at night.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.nap.summ: Short naps under 20 minutes can boost alertness without causing sleep inertia or disrupting nighttime sleep.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.red_flag: If you snore loudly and feel unrefreshed despite adequate sleep duration, ask your doctor about a sleep study.

Loud, habitual snoring with witnessed breathing pauses suggests possible sleep apnea, which affects 10-30% of adults and requires medical diagnosis. Restless legs, chronic pain disrupting sleep, and sleep disturbance tied to mood episodes also warrant professional evaluation.
Some sleep symptoms warrant medical evaluation before self-guided approaches.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.sleep_cy: Use 90-minute windows as a rough guide, not a rigid rule. Consistency of wake time matters more.

NREM-REM cycles do follow a roughly 90-minute rhythm, but the first cycle of the night is often shorter (~70 min) with more deep sleep, while later cycles are longer (~100-120 min) with more REM. Waking up naturally often occurs from REM and can feel restorative.
Sleep cycles average about 90 minutes, but the range is 70-120 minutes, and they change across the night.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.stimulus: If you lie awake for 20+ minutes, get up and do something boring in dim light.

When people spend time awake in bed (worrying, working, watching shows), the brain learns that bed is a place for wakefulness. Stimulus control therapy breaks this cycle by prescribing: only go to bed when sleepy, get up if awake for 20+ minutes, and use the bed only for sleep.
One of the most effective CBT-I techniques: re-associate the bed with sleep only.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.temperat: Try a warm bath or shower 1-2 hours before bed. Keep the bedroom slightly cool.

The body's thermoregulatory system is closely linked to sleep regulation. Vasodilation in hands and feet (which is why warm hands help sleep onset) facilitates heat loss. A warm bath 1-2 hours before bed paradoxically helps by drawing blood to the skin surface, triggering a rebound temperature drop.
A drop in core body temperature of about 1°C is required to initiate and maintain sleep.
Core body temperature and sleep onset
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.white_no: Set white noise at a comfortable volume, just loud enough to mask background disturbances.

White noise raises the auditory threshold, making it harder for sudden sounds (door closing, traffic, neighbor noise) to trigger a waking response. The effect is most pronounced in environments with intermittent noise rather than continuous noise.
White noise can help by masking sudden environmental noises that cause micro-arousals.
ref.toolbox.sleep.library.topic.worry_un: Write down your top worry and one gentler way to see it before turning off the light.

Pre-sleep cognitive arousal—worrying, planning, replaying events—is a primary driver of sleep-onset insomnia. Structured "worry time" earlier in the evening plus a brief bedside unloading exercise (writing down the top concern and a gentle reframe) reduces the mental activation that delays sleep.
A brief structured writing exercise before bed can reduce pre-sleep cognitive arousal.

ref.toolbox.sound.focus.controlMeterDesc: Sets strong/weak beat structure and subdivision density.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.controlMixDesc: Adjust accent, regular, subdivision, and vibration levels.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.controlMixDesc2: Fine-tune accent, regular, subdivision beats and vibration.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.controlTapHint: Tap to start or stop — stay in flow.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.controlTempoDesc: Adjust BPM with quick step buttons.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.controlTimbreDes: Choose the sound character for each beat click.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.immersiveControl: Tap the bottom edge to bring up controls while staying fullscreen.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.immersiveHint: Tap to start the beat. Stay in flow.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.meterDesc: Time signature sets strong/weak beats; subdivision splits each beat internally.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.mixHapticDesc: Subtle vibration on accents and section changes.
ref.toolbox.sound.focus.styleDesc: Animation and timbre are paired by default. Switch freely to mix and match.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.clear_steelcore: Clear steel-core tone tuned for rhythmic strumming.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.desktop_layout_: The strum surface stays primary while chords, capo, and tone controls sit around it.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.longer_shimmer_: Longer shimmer and overtones for ambient layers.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.phone_layout_su: The phone layout keeps the strum surface primary and moves harmony controls into compact rows.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.pick_a_chord_pl: Pick a chord, pluck or sweep the strings, and move the capo to lift the voicing.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.resonance_shape: Resonance shapes body response and pick position shifts brightness.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.rounder_and_sof: Rounder and softer for slow arpeggios and finger picking.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.shortens_sustai: Shortens sustain and tightens upper harmonics for rhythmic strokes.
ref.toolbox.sound.guitar.swipe_verticall: Swipe vertically to strum; tap a string to pluck single notes.
ref.toolbox.sound.harp.damping_sweep_dea: Damping, sweep deadzone, and chord root.
ref.toolbox.sound.harp.round_body_with_c: Round body with controlled hall tail.
ref.toolbox.sound.harp.tap_a_note_then_g: Tap a note, then glide across strings to sweep.
ref.toolbox.sound.harp.tap_for_single_no: Tap for single note, swipe for sweep.
ref.toolbox.sound.harp.tight_transient_a: Tight transient and clear note separation.
ref.toolbox.sound.harp.timbre_scale_chor: Timbre, scale, chord, and feel live in the sheet.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.confirm_locked: Source area confirmed from multiple positions. For complex environments, taking one more opposite-side sample is still recommended.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.confirm_tentat: Early clues found, but at least 3 positions are needed before a stable confirmation.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.confirm_tracki: Source area is converging. Keep the target sound active and add one more position.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.confirm_unconf: Record your current position first, then move in different directions to continue sampling.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.cue_back: Next: step back for a comparison sample, then record.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.cue_forward: Next: move one step toward the target area, then record.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.cue_left: Next: step left, keep the phone facing the same way, then record.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.cue_right: Next: step right, keep the phone facing the same way, then record.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.cue_stay: Next: keep the target active and record this spot once more.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.cue_step_0: Step 1: stay here, point the phone toward the suspected area, and record once.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_idle: Start listening, keep the target sound active, then record this position.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_low_s: SNR is low. In multi-source scenes, keep the target source continuous before locking.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_mono: Mono is still usable: record this spot, then move left, right, or forward and sample again.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_norma: Direction is updating. Record multiple positions so strength, SNR, and bearing stability can confirm the area.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_rever: Reverb risk is high. Move closer to the source, avoid corners, or lower background noise.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.mic_sufficient: The built-in phone mic is enough for movement confirmation: one static point is weak, but several positions can converge on the source area.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.no_stable_sour: No stable source yet. Keep the target source active for 1-2 seconds.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.odas_default_p: The default path is phone movement sampling; advanced mode can read ODAS tracked-source JSON as extra evidence.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.odas_descripti: External synchronized mics are not required. ODAS stays optional: if a dedicated array exists, its output can be merged into this confirmation model.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.page_subtitle: Use the phone microphone, move through several positions, and confirm the source area step by step.
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.requirement_1: Phone mic permission and stable PCM capture
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.requirement_2: At least 3 movement samples from different positions
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.requirement_3: Target sound remains active while sampling
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.requirement_4: Optional ODAS or array output as advanced evidence
ref.toolbox.sound.locator.try_stereo_sub: If the platform returns mono or fails to start, turn this off for stable activity checks.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.aggressiveOneHan: On narrow phones, enlarge black-key hit zones, reduce control density, and prefer a single keyboard.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.brightStageDesc: Sharper hammer edge for lead lines and brighter attacks.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.compactKeyboardM: Shrink key height and show more octaves to reduce frequent range switching.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.concertHallDesc: Balanced sustain and room feel for all-purpose playing.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.feltRoomDesc: Softer felt body for intimate and quiet playing.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.glissandoGuide: Single-finger glissando is supported, while two-finger vertical drags jump registers and horizontal drags switch windows.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.glissandoGuideCo: Use one finger for glissando, two fingers to change range, and tap once to switch high or low rows in phone dual mode.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.glissTip: Gliss with one finger; shift range with two.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.glissTipWide: Gliss with one finger; use two fingers to shift range.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.octaveSpanDesc: The vertical stage currently shows {octaveSpan} octaves and supports quick range switching and wrapped rows.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.sensitivityTip: Lower values are more sensitive, higher values are steadier. Fine-tune on a real device.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.studioUprightDes: Dryer wood resonance and cleaner attacks, closer to a real upright piano.
ref.toolbox.sound.piano.verticalKeyboard: The keyboard now expands down the phone height instead of being crushed horizontally.
Phone layout prioritizes one-hand taps and glissando before exposing the dual keyboard.
ref.toolbox.sound.soothing.browse_modes_: Selecting a mode closes the menu and keeps the current mode clearly highlighted.
ref.toolbox.sound.soothing.empty_mode_su: Mark modes you use often and they will appear here for quick switching.
Once you switch or play a few modes, your recent history will appear here.
ref.toolbox.sound.soothing.page_subtitle: Curated calming loops with breathing light effects, local tracks, and a mobile-first immersive layout.
ref.toolbox.sound.soothing.playback_orde: Single loop is the default. Switch to arrangement mode to auto-advance across themes and tracks.
ref.toolbox.sound.soothing.save_arrangem: Save the current arrangement for quick reuse.
ref.toolbox.sound.triangle.balanced_brig: Balanced brightness and decay close to orchestral behavior.
ref.toolbox.sound.triangle.brighter_atta: Brighter attack and stronger ring to mark accents.
ref.toolbox.sound.triangle.left_is_softe: Left is softer, right is brighter; roll mode creates tight repeated accents.
ref.toolbox.sound.triangle.material_shap: Material shapes overtones while strike point and damping control attack and tail.
ref.toolbox.sound.triangle.presets_move_: Presets move tone, material, and default ring length together.
ref.toolbox.sound.triangle.softer_highs_: Softer highs and a shorter tail for gentle rhythm support.
ref.toolbox.sound.triangle.tap_directly_: Tap directly on the triangle: left is softer, right is brighter, and the mode changes the gesture output.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.balanced_solo_t: Balanced solo tone for melodic glides.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.brighter_harmon: Brighter harmonics with a cleaner edge for airy textures.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.desktop_subtitl: Slide horizontally for pitch, vertically for strings, and now start instantly on tap.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.expose_bow_pres: Expose bow pressure and reverb separately for better solo and room control.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.phone_subtitle: Tap to start the bow, slide for pitch, and release to stop on phones.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.softer_bow_pres: Softer bow pressure with a longer tail for lyrical lines.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.use_scale_categ: Use scale categories and position windows to keep the fingerboard playable on phones.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.variant_a_is_wo: Variant A is woodier and fuller for natural solo phrases.
ref.toolbox.sound.violin.variant_b_is_br: Variant B is brighter and more forward for cutting solo lines.

toolbox.breathing.advanced_bolt_body: Your BOLT is over 40 s, indicating strong breathing efficiency. You are ready for altitude simulation and advanced hold training.
toolbox.breathing.advanced_bolt_next: You can try altitude simulation and longer breath-hold sessions. Keep up regular practice.
toolbox.breathing.altitude_extra_warning: Altitude simulation is not medical advice. Stop immediately and return to natural breathing if you feel dizzy, tightness, or any discomfort.
toolbox.breathing.altitude_simulation_de: Altitude simulation adjusts patterns and difficulty, designed for experienced users. If you have respiratory conditions, cardiovascular issues, or are pregnant, consult a doctor first.
toolbox.breathing.bolt_description: Measures your CO2 tolerance to help assess current breathing efficiency. A low score often points to shallow or rapid breathing.
toolbox.breathing.breath_hold_off: Off: best for first-time practice or when you prefer no extra hold.
toolbox.breathing.breath_hold_on: On: adding a hold makes the cycle more complete but takes more adaptation.
toolbox.breathing.building_bolt_body: Your BOLT is 20-29 s, in the building range. Breathing efficiency still has room to grow.
toolbox.breathing.building_bolt_next: Keep practicing diaphragmatic breathing and no-hold slow patterns to gradually improve CO2 tolerance.
toolbox.breathing.haptics_on: On: a light vibration on each stage change.
toolbox.breathing.low_bolt_body: Your BOLT is low (under 20 s), suggesting room to improve CO2 tolerance. Shallow or rapid breathing is a common cause.
toolbox.breathing.low_bolt_next: Start with the diaphragmatic breathing scenario and aim to raise BOLT above 20 before trying breath-hold patterns.
toolbox.breathing.not_tested_body: You have not completed a BOLT test yet. BOLT (Body Oxygen Level Test) measures your CO2 tolerance: a higher score generally indicates better breathing efficiency.
toolbox.breathing.not_tested_next: Suggestion: complete one BOLT test for a baseline score.
toolbox.breathing.recovery_off: Off: skip the recovery pause for a tighter rhythm.
toolbox.breathing.recovery_on: On: a quiet recovery pause at the end of each cycle.
toolbox.breathing.safety_note_body: Breathing exercises are not a substitute for medical advice. Consult a doctor before starting new training if you have respiratory or cardiovascular concerns or are pregnant. Stop immediately and return to natural breathing if you feel dizzy, tightness, or any discomfort.
toolbox.breathing.scenarios_subtitle: From focus to relaxation, from daily practice to BOLT testing and altitude simulation. Each scenario includes detailed breathing guidance and phase breakdown.
toolbox.breathing.stable_bolt_body: Your BOLT is 30-39 s, a stable range where breath-hold patterns become appropriate.
toolbox.breathing.stable_bolt_next: You can safely try box breathing, 4-7-8, and other patterns with holds.
toolbox.breathing.text_off: Off: rely on animation and voice only.
toolbox.breathing.text_on: On: show text prompts beside the orb.
toolbox.breathing.voice_off: Off: keep text, animation, and haptics only.
toolbox.breathing.voice_on: On: spoken reminders guide each phase of the breath.
toolbox.breathing.voice_only_chinese_bod: Breathing voice guidance is currently recorded in Chinese only. The interface can stay in your current language, but spoken cues will play in Chinese.
toolbox.daily_choice.base_rates_high_unc: Use base rates when uncertainty is high
toolbox.daily_choice.bias_noise_control_: Avoid getting dragged around by anchors, sunk costs, compelling stories, or group noise.
toolbox.daily_choice.calibrated_forecast: This is not machine learning; it is a disciplined pull back from extremes.
Average score + confidence × (raw forecast − average forecast).
Shrink extreme forecasts back toward the mean to curb overconfidence.
toolbox.daily_choice.check_guardrails_fi: Check the safety threshold before chasing upside.
toolbox.daily_choice.classify_first_subt: High-quality decisions start by identifying the type of decision before choosing the math lens.
toolbox.daily_choice.common_scale: Use a common scale to reduce noise
toolbox.daily_choice.context_influences: The context changes which lens should lead: random, weighted, scenario, or guardrails.
toolbox.daily_choice.decision_to_action: A decision must end in action
toolbox.daily_choice.expected_value_caut: Your inputs are still judgments, so estimate independently first.
toolbox.daily_choice.expected_value_form: Success probability × upside − downside exposure − effort cost.
toolbox.daily_choice.expected_value_subt: Best for uncertain outcomes when you can estimate rough odds.
toolbox.daily_choice.frame_question_righ: Clarify what is being decided, the time horizon, and which constraints are non-negotiable. A bad frame corrupts later analysis.
toolbox.daily_choice.generate_options: Generate at least 2 to 3 viable options
toolbox.daily_choice.generate_options_bo: Many bad decisions happen because the option set was poor, not because comparison failed. Expand first, then narrow.
toolbox.daily_choice.good_story: A good story is not strong evidence
toolbox.daily_choice.guardrail_best_for: Best when stakes are high, reversal is hard, time is tight, or the floor must be protected.
toolbox.daily_choice.high_stakes_guardra: For high-stakes calls, check the safety threshold before upside. Open the full checklist when needed.
When mistakes are costly to unwind, check risk, confidence, info gaps, and reversibility before chasing upside.
High stakes or hard to undo: set a safety threshold first
toolbox.daily_choice.high_uncertainty_pe: High uncertainty: bring in the pessimistic case
When you know you do not know enough, a single score is not enough. Use joint probability, scenarios, and information value together.
toolbox.daily_choice.hub_subtitle: Turn everyday small dilemmas into randomized, editable, reviewable lightweight choices.
toolbox.daily_choice.joint_probability_c: Great for multi-step dependence, weaker when the events are strongly correlated.
toolbox.daily_choice.joint_probability_f: Success probability × execution probability × confidence, then subtract downside exposure.
toolbox.daily_choice.joint_probability_s: Use a conservative product when success needs multiple things to line up.
toolbox.daily_choice.low_stakes_fast: Low stakes and reversible: decide fast
toolbox.daily_choice.low_stakes_fast_bod: For restaurants, weekend plans, or lightweight purchases, the point is not perfection. Random choice or weighted factors are usually enough.
toolbox.daily_choice.most_likely_flip: Collect the one fact most likely to change the answer
toolbox.daily_choice.no_double_down: Do not double down on sunk cost
toolbox.daily_choice.page_subtitle: Turn everyday indecision into light, editable, reviewable choices, from what to eat and wear to lightweight decision calculations.
toolbox.daily_choice.pre_commit_scan: Before committing, scan bias, noise, and review conditions.
toolbox.daily_choice.premortem: Run a premortem for high-stakes choices
toolbox.daily_choice.premortem_high_stak: Run a premortem for high stakes
toolbox.daily_choice.probability_uncerta: Translate emotional certainty into probability language that can actually be compared.
toolbox.daily_choice.professional_judgme: Medical, legal, and financial calls still need experts
toolbox.daily_choice.pull_extremes_back: Pull extreme forecasts back toward the mean
toolbox.daily_choice.regret_balance_caut: This lens corrects emotion; it does not predict destiny.
toolbox.daily_choice.regret_balance_form: Realized upside plus reversibility buffer minus regret exposure and opportunity cost.
toolbox.daily_choice.regret_balance_subt: Useful when you are likely to revisit the decision and ask what you should have chosen.
toolbox.daily_choice.research_flip_fact: Research the fact most likely to change the answer
toolbox.daily_choice.same_fields: Use the same fields for every option
toolbox.daily_choice.scenario_blend_caut: When uncertainty is high, let the pessimistic case carry real weight.
toolbox.daily_choice.scenario_blend_form: A weighted blend of optimistic, base, and pessimistic cases.
toolbox.daily_choice.scenario_blend_subt: Blend optimistic, base, and pessimistic scenarios so you do not stare only at the upside.
toolbox.daily_choice.six_elements_qualit: Taken from the Stanford decision-quality framework. This is the backbone of the module.
toolbox.daily_choice.stop_rule_now: If you must decide now, define a stopping rule
toolbox.daily_choice.sunk_cost: Sunk cost is not a reason to continue
toolbox.daily_choice.threshold_guardrail: In high-stakes situations, protect the floor before chasing upside.
Check confidence, downside, reversibility, and info gaps first, then break ties with a composite score.
Check minimum standards first, then rank only the options that clear them.
toolbox.daily_choice.uniform_random_caut: Do not use random choice for high-stakes decisions.
toolbox.daily_choice.uniform_random_form: Each option gets the same chance. The goal is to end hesitation fast.
toolbox.daily_choice.uniform_random_subt: Best for low-stakes, reversible choices with tiny differences.
toolbox.daily_choice.use_multiplication: Use multiplication when several conditions must hold
toolbox.daily_choice.value_ranking_disag: Return to value ranking when methods disagree
toolbox.daily_choice.weather_not_ready: Showing all temperatures for now. If the weather service has loaded, it will be used here automatically.
toolbox.daily_choice.weighted_factors_ca: Useful for ranking, not for claiming certainty.
toolbox.daily_choice.weighted_factors_fo: Weighted positives minus penalties for risk, effort, regret, and info gaps.
toolbox.daily_choice.weighted_factors_su: Compare value, success odds, reversibility, risk, and info gaps on one ruler.
toolbox.daily_choice.when_to_research: When to research more and when to move
toolbox.daily_choice.when_to_research_su: Information has value, but analysis still needs a stop point.

toolbox.sleep.library.advice_assessment_: Based on your sensitivity, set a firm caffeine cutoff 8-10 hours before your typical bedtime to protect your natural sleep pressure.

A cool, dark, and quiet bedroom supports the natural drop in core body temperature needed for sleep.

Your assessment suggests an irregular sleep schedule. A structured rhythm program focusing on consistent wake time and morning light can stabilize your circadian rhythm.

Your assessment flagged potential risk factors that may benefit from professional evaluation alongside self-guided approaches.

A warm bath 1-2 hours before bed, plus a cool bedroom, helps trigger the core temperature drop needed for sleep.

Even a simple 3-step pre-bed routine can significantly reduce the time it takes to fall asleep by signaling to your brain that the day is ending.

toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_caffe: Your logs show caffeine consumption close to bedtime on some nights. Even when you can fall asleep, caffeine reduces deep sleep.
Caffeine after the cutoff can fragment sleep architecture even without delaying sleep onset.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_envir: Your logs show environmental factors are affecting your sleep. Small adjustments to temperature, light, or noise can make a meaningful difference.
The bedroom environment directly impacts the body's ability to initiate and maintain sleep.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_light: Your sleep quality correlates with morning light exposure. Try getting outside for 10-15 minutes within 30 minutes of waking.
Morning light is the strongest zeitgeber for anchoring circadian rhythm.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_minim: Your daily log entries are building a dataset that reveals patterns. Keep going — even 30-second entries add up.
Sleep diary data over multiple nights reveals patterns that single-night snapshots miss.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_nap.b: Your data suggests daytime sleepiness. If you nap, keep it under 20 minutes and before 3pm. If you have insomnia, consider skipping naps.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_nap.r: Naps can help or hurt nighttime sleep depending on timing and duration.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_rescu: Night awakenings appear in your recent logs. Having a pre-planned low-stimulation response makes it easier to handle them calmly.
A planned response to night waking reduces the anxiety and clock-checking that prolong wakefulness.
Keep the night rescue tool handy
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_scree: Late screen use appears in your recent logs. Switching to night mode or putting devices away 30-60 minutes before bed can improve sleep quality.
Evening blue light can suppress melatonin and delay sleep onset.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_daily_worry: Pre-sleep worry or busy-mind patterns show in your data. A 2-minute writing exercise before bed can significantly reduce this cognitive arousal.
Pre-sleep cognitive arousal is a primary driver of sleep-onset difficulty.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_weekly_caff: Caffeine close to bedtime correlates with lower sleep efficiency and less deep sleep in your weekly data.

Your caffeine pattern may be reducing sleep quality
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_weekly_envi: Environmental complaints (temperature, noise, light) appear across multiple nights. Consistent bedroom optimization can yield cumulative benefits.
Persistent environmental issues have a compounding negative effect on sleep quality.
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_weekly_ligh: Your weekly data shows inconsistent morning light. Prioritizing even 10 minutes outdoors within 30 minutes of waking can strengthen your sleep-wake cycle.
Consistent morning light exposure is the most effective way to stabilize circadian timing.
Morning light is your strongest rhythm tool
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_weekly_resc: Multiple night awakenings in your recent logs suggest having a pre-planned rescue response could help. The key: avoid clock-checking, and get up briefly if awake 20+ minutes.
A planned response to night waking reduces the frustration that can prolong wakefulness.
Night awakenings: prepare a response plan
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_weekly_scre: Your data shows a correlation between late screen use and longer time to fall asleep. Try a 30-60 minute screen-free buffer before bed.
Screen light and content arousal both contribute to delayed sleep onset.
Late screen use is affecting your sleep
toolbox.sleep.library.advice_weekly_slee: Your weekly sleep duration shows variability. Focus on consistent wake time rather than bedtime — this is the stronger anchor for circadian rhythm.

toolbox.sleep.library.topic.bedroom.acti: Keep the bedroom cool, dark, and quiet. Try a temperature of 18-20°C.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.bedroom.deta: The ideal bedroom temperature for sleep is 18-20°C (65-68°F). Core body temperature must drop by about 1°C to initiate and maintain sleep. A room that is too warm prevents this drop. Noise above 40dB can cause arousals even without full awakening.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.bedroom.summ: Temperature, noise, and light are the three main environmental factors affecting sleep quality.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.caffeine.act: Set a personal caffeine cutoff 8-10 hours before your typical bedtime.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.caffeine.det: Adenosine builds up during the day, creating "sleep pressure." Caffeine temporarily blocks adenosine receptors, masking sleepiness without reducing the underlying pressure. Genetic differences in CYP1A2 mean some people metabolize caffeine much slower than others.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.caffeine.sum: Caffeine works by blocking adenosine receptors. Its half-life is 3-7 hours, meaning a 2pm coffee can still affect sleep at midnight.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.diary_trends: Log just 3 data points per night: bedtime, wake time, and how rested you feel.

Consumer sleep trackers estimate sleep stages from movement and heart rate, but their accuracy varies widely and they often overestimate sleep. A simple diary capturing bedtime, wake time, and subjective restfulness provides complementary data that highlights behavioral patterns trackers cannot see.
A 30-second sleep log reveals patterns that even detailed sleep trackers miss.
The power of a simple sleep diary
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.digital_suns: Switch devices to night mode after sunset. Stop active screen use 30-60 minutes before bed.

The melanopsin photopigment in ipRGC cells is most sensitive to ~480nm (blue) light. Evening exposure shifts the circadian clock later, making it harder to fall asleep. However, the effect size varies widely between individuals, and content arousal may matter as much as the light itself.
Evening screen light, especially blue wavelengths, can suppress melatonin by activating the same ipRGC cells that respond to morning light.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.light.action: Get outside within 30 minutes of waking. No sunglasses for the first 10 minutes.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.light.detail: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) uses light detected by ipRGC cells in the retina to synchronize your circadian rhythm. Morning light advances your clock, making it easier to fall asleep at night. Even 10-15 minutes outdoors on a cloudy day provides enough lux to make a measurable difference.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.light.summar: Bright light within 30 minutes of waking is the single strongest signal for your internal clock.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.light.title: Morning light and circadian anchoring
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.nap.action_h: Naps under 20 minutes, before 3pm. If you have insomnia, skip naps entirely.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.nap.detail: The ideal nap window is 10-20 minutes (the "power nap") which stays in lighter NREM sleep stages before entering deep slow-wave sleep. Longer naps (30+ min) risk sleep inertia—grogginess on waking—and can reduce homeostatic sleep pressure, making it harder to fall asleep at night.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.nap.summary: Short naps under 20 minutes can boost alertness without causing sleep inertia or disrupting nighttime sleep.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.nap.title: Naps: strategic use and timing
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.red_flags.ac: If you snore loudly and feel unrefreshed despite adequate sleep duration, ask your doctor about a sleep study.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.red_flags.de: Loud, habitual snoring with witnessed breathing pauses suggests possible sleep apnea, which affects 10-30% of adults and requires medical diagnosis. Restless legs, chronic pain disrupting sleep, and sleep disturbance tied to mood episodes also warrant professional evaluation.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.red_flags.su: Some sleep symptoms warrant medical evaluation before self-guided approaches.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.sleep_cycles: Use 90-minute windows as a rough guide, not a rigid rule. Consistency of wake time matters more.

NREM-REM cycles do follow a roughly 90-minute rhythm, but the first cycle of the night is often shorter (~70 min) with more deep sleep, while later cycles are longer (~100-120 min) with more REM. Waking up naturally often occurs from REM and can feel restorative.
Sleep cycles average about 90 minutes, but the range is 70-120 minutes, and they change across the night.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.stimulus_con: If you lie awake for 20+ minutes, get up and do something boring in dim light.

When people spend time awake in bed (worrying, working, watching shows), the brain learns that bed is a place for wakefulness. Stimulus control therapy breaks this cycle by prescribing: only go to bed when sleepy, get up if awake for 20+ minutes, and use the bed only for sleep.
One of the most effective CBT-I techniques: re-associate the bed with sleep only.
Try a warm bath or shower 1-2 hours before bed. Keep the bedroom slightly cool.

The body's thermoregulatory system is closely linked to sleep regulation. Vasodilation in hands and feet (which is why warm hands help sleep onset) facilitates heat loss. A warm bath 1-2 hours before bed paradoxically helps by drawing blood to the skin surface, triggering a rebound temperature drop.
A drop in core body temperature of about 1°C is required to initiate and maintain sleep.
Core body temperature and sleep onset
Set white noise at a comfortable volume, just loud enough to mask background disturbances.

White noise raises the auditory threshold, making it harder for sudden sounds (door closing, traffic, neighbor noise) to trigger a waking response. The effect is most pronounced in environments with intermittent noise rather than continuous noise.
White noise can help by masking sudden environmental noises that cause micro-arousals.
toolbox.sleep.library.topic.worry_unload: Write down your top worry and one gentler way to see it before turning off the light.

Pre-sleep cognitive arousal—worrying, planning, replaying events—is a primary driver of sleep-onset insomnia. Structured "worry time" earlier in the evening plus a brief bedside unloading exercise (writing down the top concern and a gentle reframe) reduces the mental activation that delays sleep.
A brief structured writing exercise before bed can reduce pre-sleep cognitive arousal.

toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_idle: Start listening, keep the target sound active, then record this position.
toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_low_snr: SNR is low. In multi-source scenes, keep the target source continuous before locking.
toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_mono: Mono is still usable: record this spot, then move left, right, or forward and sample again.
toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_normal: Direction is updating. Record multiple positions so strength, SNR, and bearing stability can confirm the area.
toolbox.sound.locator.guidance_reverb: Reverb risk is high. Move closer to the source, avoid corners, or lower background noise.
toolbox.sound.locator.mic_sufficient: The built-in phone mic is enough for movement confirmation: one static point is weak, but several positions can converge on the source area.
toolbox.sound.locator.no_stable_source: No stable source yet. Keep the target source active for 1-2 seconds.
toolbox.sound.locator.odas_default_path: The default path is phone movement sampling; advanced mode can read ODAS tracked-source JSON as extra evidence.
toolbox.sound.locator.odas_description: External synchronized mics are not required. ODAS stays optional: if a dedicated array exists, its output can be merged into this confirmation model.
toolbox.sound.locator.page_subtitle: Use the phone microphone, move through several positions, and confirm the source area step by step.
toolbox.sound.locator.requirement_1: Phone mic permission and stable PCM capture
toolbox.sound.locator.requirement_2: At least 3 movement samples from different positions
toolbox.sound.locator.requirement_3: Target sound remains active while sampling
toolbox.sound.locator.requirement_4: Optional ODAS or array output as advanced evidence
toolbox.sound.locator.try_stereo_subtitl: If the platform returns mono or fails to start, turn this off for stable activity checks.
toolbox.sound.piano.aggressiveOneHandDes: On narrow phones, enlarge black-key hit zones, reduce control density, and prefer a single keyboard.
toolbox.sound.piano.brightStageDesc: Sharper hammer edge for lead lines and brighter attacks.
toolbox.sound.piano.compactKeyboardModeD: Shrink key height and show more octaves to reduce frequent range switching.
toolbox.sound.piano.concertHallDesc: Balanced sustain and room feel for all-purpose playing.
toolbox.sound.piano.dualModeDesc: Show two adjacent ranges and play on both keyboards with two fingers.
toolbox.sound.piano.duetModeDesc: In dual mode, two people can play on high and low keyboards simultaneously.
toolbox.sound.piano.feltRoomDesc: Softer felt body for intimate and quiet playing.
toolbox.sound.piano.gestureSwitchingDesc: Swipe up or down with two fingers to switch ranges quickly. Disable if conflict occurs.
toolbox.sound.piano.glissandoGuide: Single-finger glissando is supported, while two-finger vertical drags jump registers and horizontal drags switch windows.
toolbox.sound.piano.glissandoGuideCompac: Use one finger for glissando, two fingers to change range, and tap once to switch high or low rows in phone dual mode.
toolbox.sound.piano.glissTip: Gliss with one finger; shift range with two.
toolbox.sound.piano.glissTipWide: Gliss with one finger; use two fingers to shift range.
toolbox.sound.piano.octaveSpanDesc: The vertical stage currently shows {octaveSpan} octaves and supports quick range switching and wrapped rows.
toolbox.sound.piano.sensitivityTip: Lower values are more sensitive, higher values are steadier. Fine-tune on a real device.
toolbox.sound.piano.studioUprightDesc: Dryer wood resonance and cleaner attacks, closer to a real upright piano.
toolbox.sound.piano.verticalKeyboardDesc: The keyboard now expands down the phone height instead of being crushed horizontally.
toolbox.sound.piano.verticalKeyboardPhon: Phone layout prioritizes one-hand taps and glissando before exposing the dual keyboard.
toolbox.sound.soothing.browse_modes_subt: Selecting a mode closes the menu and keeps the current mode clearly highlighted.
toolbox.sound.soothing.empty_mode_subtit: Mark modes you use often and they will appear here for quick switching.
Once you switch or play a few modes, your recent history will appear here.
toolbox.sound.soothing.page_subtitle: Curated calming loops with breathing light effects, local tracks, and a mobile-first immersive layout.
toolbox.sound.soothing.playback_order_de: Single loop is the default. Switch to arrangement mode to auto-advance across themes and tracks.
toolbox.sound.soothing.save_arrangement_: Save the current arrangement for quick reuse.
toolbox.sound.triangle.balanced_brightne: Balanced brightness and decay close to orchestral behavior.
toolbox.sound.triangle.brighter_attack_a: Brighter attack and stronger ring to mark accents.
toolbox.sound.triangle.left_is_softer_ri: Left is softer, right is brighter; roll mode creates tight repeated accents.
toolbox.sound.triangle.material_shapes_o: Material shapes overtones while strike point and damping control attack and tail.
toolbox.sound.triangle.presets_move_tone: Presets move tone, material, and default ring length together.
toolbox.sound.triangle.softer_highs_and_: Softer highs and a shorter tail for gentle rhythm support.
toolbox.sound.triangle.tap_directly_on_t: Tap directly on the triangle: left is softer, right is brighter, and the mode changes the gesture output.
toolbox.sound.violin.balanced_solo_tone_: Balanced solo tone for melodic glides.
toolbox.sound.violin.brighter_harmonics_: Brighter harmonics with a cleaner edge for airy textures.
toolbox.sound.violin.desktop_subtitle: Slide horizontally for pitch, vertically for strings, and now start instantly on tap.
toolbox.sound.violin.expose_bow_pressure: Expose bow pressure and reverb separately for better solo and room control.
toolbox.sound.violin.phone_subtitle: Tap to start the bow, slide for pitch, and release to stop on phones.
toolbox.sound.violin.softer_bow_pressure: Softer bow pressure with a longer tail for lyrical lines.
toolbox.sound.violin.use_scale_categorie: Use scale categories and position windows to keep the fingerboard playable on phones.
toolbox.sound.violin.variant_a_is_woodie: Variant A is woodier and fuller for natural solo phrases.
toolbox.sound.violin.variant_b_is_bright: Variant B is brighter and more forward for cutting solo lines.
